reviews.claim: Creating dynamic and physically realistic 4D worlds from natural language descriptions is both fascinating and challenging. Traditional computer graphics methods rely on manual creation, requiring extensive human effort to fine-tune materials, motions, and visual fidelity.
reviews.mechanism: We present GS-Agent, an end-to-end multi-agent framework that integrates physics engines in the loop to generate realistic, dynamic, and controllable 4D physical worlds from natural language.
method_locators: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.21522v1#S3 — 3 GS-Agent: A Multi-Agent Framework with Generative Simulation in the Loop
https://arxiv.org/html/2607.21522v1#A2 — Appendix B Additional Implementation Details

reviews.claim: Concurrent stateful library APIs expose behavior through evolving resource ownership, lifecycle states, and competing interleavings. reviews.claim: While large audio-language models have achieved remarkable progress in auditory perception, they still lag behind text-based large language models in deep logical reasoning, primarily due to the scarcity of high-quality audio reasoning data. reviews.claim: Modern AI agents rely on elaborate inference harnesses such as Claude Code, Codex, and OpenClaw to drive multi-turn reasoning, tool use, and access to external systems. While powerful, these complex harnesses also make agents hard to train end-to-end with open infrastructure, whose SFT/RL stacks cannot natively express stateful, multi-process harness inference.
reviews.mechanism: To address this, we present OpenForgeRL, an open-source framework for training harness-based agents end-to-end in diverse environments.

reviews.claim: Understanding motion in video is a fundamental challenge for visual learning, as frame-to-frame change entangles two sources of dynamics: camera motion and object motion. This decomposition has remained underexplored in representation learning, partly because these factors are tightly coupled in natural videos and difficult to supervise separately.
reviews.mechanism: We propose the Structured Dynamics Model (SDM), which explicitly separates the dominant source of temporal change from residual dynamics through future-feature prediction, rather than representing video change with a single entangled latent or with unstructured, spatially dense transition tokens.
evaluation_locators: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.21576v1#A1 — Appendix A Dataset and Evaluation Details

reviews.proved: These results suggest that pretrained image models can be readily repurposed into structured video-dynamics representations, providing a useful inductive bias for learning and analyzing latent video dynamics.

reviews.claim: Flow-based generative models have enabled remarkable progress in fast and controllable generation across continuous and discrete state spaces, yet existing parameterizations are constrained to fixed dimensions or fixed sequence lengths.
